title: His Lifeline Snapped 100 m Under the North Sea

lines.text: His lifeline snapped nearly a hundred metres under the North Sea.
He had about five minutes of gas on his back.
Chris Lemons, a saturation diver, was working on the seabed.
Above him, his support ship's positioning system failed.
His umbilical, carrying his gas and his radio, snagged on steel.
In total darkness, he pulled himself back to the structure.
Then his emergency gas ran out.
It would take around half an hour to reach him.
When Dave Yuasa got there, Lemons was unresponsive.
He hauled him back into the diving bell.
There, Duncan Allcock gave him rescue breaths.
And Chris Lemons started breathing again.
Near-freezing water chilled him, slowing his brain's need for oxygen.
Three weeks later, he was back at work.

shots.environment: other:subsea manifold structure on the seabed (low-poly steel frame 6x4x3 m, pipe spools, valves; seabed builder underneath)
shots.description: Mid-story from frame 1: a stylised diver kneels on top of the steel manifold in green-black water. Behind him the umbilical (thick emissive cyan tube, guideline builder, thickness 0.04) is pulled taut upward into darkness, then whips and snaps; its glowing end recoils and the glow dies along its length. A small burst of bubbles from the break.
